title: 2 · Forging temperature window
summary: The same gear blank forged at four temperatures: how much press do you save by forging hotter?
instructions: 1. Press Solve once to see the baseline at 1150 °C: the load rises sharply in the last millimetres when the flash forms.
2. Run its multi-run (1000 → 1225 °C). Each run is added to RUNS and overlaid on the chart.
3. Compare the peak loads in the RUNS list. Hotter = softer steel (C(T) falls about 0.3 % per °C) = lower load; the fill barely changes.
4. Save all… writes one CSV per run plus summary.csv (peak load vs temperature) for a spreadsheet chart.
5. Discussion: why not forge even hotter? (scale, grain growth, die life: outside this model).
